ai.title: Tighten terminal command safety and timeout guidance in system prompt
ai.summary: The system prompt for the `run_terminal_command` tool was updated to enforce stricter safety guidelines and clarify execution constraints. A 30-second timeout limit was explicitly added, prohibiting long-running or server-starting commands. Instructions regarding script execution were hardened, requiring explicit user permission for actions with permanent effects or significant environmental changes like installing global packages or virtual environments. Redundant references to grep/find and test script examples were removed or simplified to focus on core safety mechanics.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to run a command in your terminal, it is now told to stop and ask you first before installing new software or setting up virtual environments. Any single command it runs will also be forced to quit after 30 seconds, so things like development servers that run forever will be refused outright. This guidance lives inside the same internal list of rules the assistant reads, so it does not change anything you see right now, but it makes sure future terminal commands are safer and quicker to run.

ai.title: Fix typos in system prompt terminal command guidance
ai.summary: Corrected text errors in backend/src/system-prompt.ts. Fixed missing parentheses in test execution example and misspelled 'globally' in permission guidelines. Internal documentation update only.

eli5.text: The assistant's written instructions for using the terminal had two small text errors that have now been corrected. The example for running tests was missing an opening parenthesis, and the word 'globally' was misspelled in a sentence about asking permission before installing things. These are internal documentation fixes only, so you wouldn't notice any difference in how the system works.

ai.title: Add onWebSocketReconnect callback to APIRealtimeClient
ai.summary: APIRealtimeClient now accepts an onReconnect callback invoked upon successful reconnection, replacing hardcoded console logging. CLI and Client classes updated to pass this callback, ensuring proper UI state reset (prompting, stopping animations) via returnControlToUser. Covers common/websocket-client.ts and npm-app client/cli implementations.

eli5.text: When you lose your internet connection during a chat and then get reconnected, the app now properly resets everything instead of just printing a message in green text. The reconnection process now clears out the old state, stops any loading animations, and puts the chat prompt back so you can type normally again, rather than leaving things in a half-frozen state where the app thinks it is still waiting for a response.

ai.title: Fix git stage condition in CLI
ai.summary: The CLI now checks `changesAlreadyApplied.length` instead of `allChanges.length` when determining whether to stage files. This corrects the logic to only trigger `stagePatches` when there are actual changes to stage, preventing unnecessary operations or errors when no changes are present. The fix is isolated to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When the product tried to set up automatic version control staging (saving your work progress), it was checking the wrong list of files - using all possible changes instead of only the ones actually new or modified. This caused it to attempt staging actions even when there was nothing new to save, sometimes producing errors or wasted operations. The fix makes it correctly check only the list of changes that are ready to be staged, so staging now happens only when there's actually something new to process.

ai.title: Anon tier limit reduced to 250 credits
ai.summary: The ANON plan configuration in common/src/constants.ts reduces the credit limit from 500 to 250. This change enforces stricter usage constraints for unauthenticated users. The modification applies globally via the shared core constants.

eli5.text: If you use the service without signing in, you now start each session with 250 free credits instead of the previous 500. This halves the amount of work you can do before being asked to create an account or upgrade. The limit is set in one shared place, so it applies everywhere the anonymous pay-as-you-go plan is used.

ai.title: Revert git stage new changes in cli.ts
ai.summary: Reverted commit fixing git staging logic in npm-app/src/cli.ts. Staging condition reverted to use allChanges instead of changesAlreadyApplied. Internal CLI logic adjustment.

eli5.text: The tool now stages all pending changes instead of only the ones it already applied, so when you run the staging command it will pick up everything sitting in your workspace rather than a smaller filtered set. This affects anyone using the internal CLI to stage changes for commit, and you'd notice that more files get staged than before when you run the command. The behavior is live right now for internal CLI users.

ai.title: Add git stage flag to Client
ai.summary: Client constructor accepts git parameter. stagePatches called before applyChanges when git equals stage. CLI passes this.git to Client. Ensures files are staged prior to modification.

eli5.text: When you ask the tool to edit files with a save-to-disk mode enabled, it now quietly puts those files into your pending-changes tray first, so they sit ready for your review before any changes are written. The tool that talks to the file-editing service now carries this save-to-disk setting along, and passes the files you're about to modify into the staging step right before editing them, so nothing gets applied unseen.

ai.title: CI typecheck scripts split into package-local and full-build variants
ai.summary: CI workflow calls `typecheck-this-package` instead of `build`/`typecheck` for backend, npm-app, and web. Each package now defines `typecheck-this-package` (tsc --noEmit + tsc-alias) and a wrapper `typecheck` that builds `common` (and `code-map` for npm-app) first. Scope: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `backend/package.json`, `npm-app/package.json`, `web/package.json`. Backend previously ran `build` (tsc --build + tsc-alias) in CI; now runs `typecheck-this-package` (tsc --noEmit + tsc-alias), aligning with other packages.

eli5.text: The automated checking system that normally builds and tests everything now skips the full build step for the backend, app, and web tools, opting instead to just check their own code without pulling in other components first. This means if you changed something in one of these packages today, the checks would run faster but won't catch integration issues with shared code until later. The shared code still gets built first, but each tool is now responsible for verifying itself independently.
